title: Evaluating consumption effects of intelligent control algorithms for district heated buildings
summary: As buildings become increasingly connected and sensor-rich, intelligent remote heating control is rapidly superseding conventional local heating control. Such control algorithms often aim at reducing energy consumption by minimizing over-heating and utilizing free solar energy, for instance. Numerous companies offering heating optimization solutions have recently emerged. After installing such a system, end-users naturally want to quantify and verify the effect of such an investment, i.e., monetary return.
